actionable_steps.citation: Hold Fast To The Lord — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 25 (1992), 1992-04-04
actionable_steps.step: Treat your senses as instruments you wield — refuse to be their plaything any longer.

actionable_steps.citation: Flowers That Never Fade — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 33 (2000), 2000-08-22
actionable_steps.step: Begin with the tongue: control its craving for delicacies, eat to sustain the body, and fill your speech with the Divine Name.

actionable_steps.citation: Flowers That Never Fade — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 33 (2000), 2000-08-22
actionable_steps.step: Tell your eyes to see God instead of unsacred things, and teach your ears to listen to the stories of the Lord instead of vain gossip.

actionable_steps.citation: Sacred use of Indhriyas — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 30 (1997), 1997-10-06
actionable_steps.step: Turn every sense toward the sacred: see good, think good thoughts, speak sweet words, listen to what is good — be good and do good.

actionable_steps.citation: God is the Embodiment of All Names and Forms — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 29 (1996), 1996-08-24
actionable_steps.step: Make sense control your top priority — it wins God's grace, and it is possible if you make the effort with firm determination.

definition.citation: Control of Senses is the Real Sadhana — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 39 (2006), 2006-02-23
definition.quote: What is mukti (liberation)? Liberation is control of the senses. Unless one controls one's senses, liberation is not possible. … Hence, controlling the senses should be your top priority.

discourses.citation: Hold Fast To The Lord — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 25 (1992), 1992-04-04
discourses.quote: Man imagines that he is making use of his sense organs. Not at all. The truth is the senses are sporting with man. … These instruments should be wielded by you. You should not become their plaything.

discourses.citation: Flowers That Never Fade — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 33 (2000), 2000-08-22
discourses.quote: All spiritual practices will prove futile if one lacks sense control. Control of the senses is very essential for one and all. Lack of sense control is the main cause of all the unrest and agitation that you find in the world today.

discourses.citation: Seek God within — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 32 (1999), 1999-11-21
discourses.quote: Sage Patanjali said, "Yogaha chtta vritti nirodaha," controlling the vagaries of the mind is yoga and allowing the senses to have their own way is roga (disease). … One should become a yogi, not a rogi.

discourses.citation: God is the Embodiment of All Names and Forms — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 29 (1996), 1996-08-24
discourses.quote: You can win God's grace (anugraha) only by sense control (indriya nigraha). Therefore, if you want God's grace, control your senses.

make_it_real: Today, catch one sense running wild — the tongue, the eyes, the ears — and put it back to its sacred use.
title: Sense Control

vahinis.quote: The sacred revelations (sruthis) say: equanimity, self-control, withdrawal of the senses, and steadfastness — only these confer that title, not caste, colour, or social status.
